jobs.title: Counsellor/Social Worker (FAM Woodlands)
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

You will be part of the team to provide casework and counselling services for families, with the goal for families to achieve healthy family functioning, and to deliver divorce support programmes and services to families who are affected by divorce, with the goal for families and their children to achieve stability and self-reliance. 

Job Roles And Responsibilities

Casework and Counselling

Part of the Intake and Triage Team to conduct intake assessments for new intakes to identify needs, strengths, and risks and make necessary referrals for clients. 
Conduct counselling for individuals, couples and families who are experiencing stress due to marital and family-related issues. Includes Online counselling.
Conduct case management for clients and case conferences with stakeholders.
Identify, assessment and manage risks inherent in low-moderate complex cases by integrating a range of information and screening tools.

Support Programme and Workshops

Plan, review and facilitate groupwork intervention for parents and children.
Facilitate premarital and divorce related programme and workshops to help equip couples and parents with knowledge that enhance relationships and skills to cope with life transitions.

Supervision

Provide programme and/ or practice/clinical supervision to junior Counsellor/Social Worker and/or interns/Contract for Service Family Life Educators to ensure programme fidelity and quality service delivery

Research and Practice

Contribute to quality practice and professional matters in agency.
Engage in research to evaluate activities and identify service gaps. 
Facilitate internal training for team / service point

Networking

Support networking and advocacy sessions with partners and stakeholders

Job Requirements

Degree in Counselling OR Degree in Social Work (preferably with a recognised certification in Counselling)
At least 3 years of relevant casework / counselling experience in counselling, social work, or related work involving family, parents and children, and have experience in conducting training and workshop
Preferably clinical member of SAC

jobs.title: Foster Care Case Manager
jobs.description:
Company Description
Sunrise Children's Services is a statewide nonprofit organization dedicated to providing care, hope, and therapeutic services to children and families across Kentucky. Since 1869, Sunrise has focused on serving children who have experienced abuse, neglect, and significant trauma and who have been removed from their homes by the state. The organization serves more than 1,000 individuals each day, offering refuge, healing, and support through a network of Christ-centered programs. Licensed as a Behavioral Health Services Organization, Sunrise provides foster care, residential treatment, therapeutic, and community-based services and holds Gold Seal accreditation from The Joint Commission. Applicants can learn more about Sunrise’s mission, programs, and statewide impact at www.sunrise.org.
Role Description
The Foster Care Case Manager is a full-time, on-site role based in Elizabethtown, KY, responsible for supporting children and foster families through comprehensive case management services. Daily responsibilities include assessing child and family needs, developing and updating individualized service plans, and coordinating placements and services with foster parents, schools, medical providers, and community partners. The role involves conducting home visits, monitoring safety and progress, documenting case activities in accordance with agency and regulatory standards, and preparing reports for court and state agencies. The Case Manager provides ongoing support, advocacy, and crisis intervention, facilitating team meetings and ensuring that services align with therapeutic goals and organizational policies. This position collaborates closely with internal clinical staff and external stakeholders to promote positive outcomes and stability for children in care.
Qualifications

Strong case management and social services skills, including assessment, service planning, coordination of care, and advocacy.
Excellent communication and documentation skills, including clear written reports, professional correspondence, and effective interpersonal communication with children, families, and partners.
Organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple cases, maintain accurate records, and meet deadlines and regulatory requirements.
Collaboration and teamwork skills, including the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams, foster parents, state agencies, and community organizations.
Knowledge of child welfare, trauma-informed care, and behavioral health principles, along with familiarity with foster care regulations and best practices.
Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, or related human services field; a master’s degree and relevant licensure (e.g., CSW, LCSW) are preferred.
Previous experience in foster care, child welfare, or related residential or community-based services is highly beneficial.
Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel locally for home visits and meetings.
Ability to maintain professional boundaries, uphold confidentiality, and align practice with Sunrise Children’s Services mission and ethical standards.

jobs.description:
Salary

$28.14 - $30.92 Hourly

Location

Missoula, Montana

Job Type

Regular, Full-Time

Description
Benefits
Questions

Overview

Make a difference where it matters most.

The City of Missoula Municipal Court is hiring a Court Case Manager
to play a key role in transforming lives by connecting individuals in the criminal justice system with the support and services they need. If you thrive on building relationships, navigating complex challenges, and advocating for positive change, this position offers a chance to do impactful work every day. From guiding defendants through discharge plans to coordinating mental health, substance use, housing, and vocational resources—you’ll be part of a team working to create safer, healthier outcomes for individuals and the community.

To Apply:

All applicants must submit the City of Missoula application

AND Cover Letter

explaining your interest in this position and detailing how your experience and education meet the qualifications.

Failure to attach the cover letter will result in your application being incomplete, and therefore, not reviewed by the hiring manager.

Priority Screening of applications will begin on Thursday, September 24, 2026.

Applicants applying on or after this date will only be considered if a competitive applicant pool is not received.

Resumes will not be reviewed. All details should be entered on the application.

Starting Pay

New hires start within our entry-to-market range, depending on experience and qualifications.

The starting range for the position is $28.14 - $30.92/hour and will increase each year for longevity and cost of living adjustments.

Full Pay Range

Each position also has a full wage range that reflects potential growth over time, including annual increases for longevity and cost-of-living.

The full range for the position is $28.14 - $32.78/hour.

Essential Functions

Meet directly with defendants pre- and post-sentencing, using established interview techniques and assessment instruments to determine programmatic needs to develop treatment plans and track defendants’ progress.
Provide defendants support through case management and offering information and/or referrals for mental health services, substance use disorder services, and other various programs/resources.
Assist with the Pretrial Assistance to Support Success (PASS) program to coordinate services for defendants’ pre-disposition to support a successful re-entry into the community following release from incarceration.
Establish a collaborative network within the community and other relevant partners to involve family members, community resources, and social service agencies to assist defendants, pre-and post-disposition, with employment and vocational skills, educational and training needs, housing, substance abuse resources, etc.
Assist the Court Program Administrator with community-based programs and other outreach initiatives by attending and providing support to participants and coordinating with other service providers to attend court-sponsored events and provide resources, as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned, based on training and qualifications.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of, or the ability to learn, local substance abuse, mental health services, and community resources, including related government laws and practices of community resources.
Knowledge of general criminal justice and case management practices and procedures, including interviewing and counseling techniques, cultural competence with awareness and respect for diversity and inclusion.
Skill in utilizing various computer software and databases, including Microsoft 365, and the ability to learn job-specific applications and equipment.
Skill in organization, time management and prioritizing with the proven ability to have keen attention to detail and accuracy in performing work with adherence to strict deadlines.
Skill in communicating, in person and writing, with the proven ability to establish and maintain effective working and collaborative relationships with diverse individuals.
Ability to motivate defendants in a positive, constructive manner; facilitating self-determination and self-care through the tenets of advocacy.
Ability to identify and resolve barriers hindering effective program participation and completion for defendants.
Ability to research, analyze, and provide decisive solutions to complex problems and situations.
Ability to maintain current knowledge, developments, and trends related to specific area of focus and/or assigned projects.
Ability to maintain and exhibit integrity and discretion in handling confidential, sensitive, and criminal justice information.
Ability to maintain and foster a culture of professionalism, adhere to departmental and City standards and specifications, and support a positive team environment.
Ability to resolve conflicts with facilitating outcomes while maintaining a calm demeanor.
Ability to learn City and departmental policies, procedures, and practices.

Qualifications And Additional Application Materials

Any combination of education and experience equivalent to four (4) years of experience working or providing case management services in behavioral health care, social services; working in a correctional facility with direct contact with clients, or another relevant field.
Must be able to pass a criminal background check.

The City of Missoula does not sponsor employment visas (e.g., F-1, H-1B, TM). Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis at the time of application.

El rol tiene como objetivo asegurar que nuestras operaciones se desarrollen bajo los más altos estándares legales, corporativos y éticos, impulsando una cultura de prevención, cumplimiento y mejora continua que proteja a nuestras personas, nuestras instalaciones y el medio ambiente.

Lo Que Realizarás

Implementar y asegurar el cumplimiento legal y regulatorio en materia de EHS (STPS, SEMARNAT, COFEPRIS), así como de los estándares ISO 14001 e ISO 45001.
Coordinar, ejecutar y dar seguimiento a los programas de EHS en planta, incluyendo contratistas, proveedores, visitantes y colaboradores.
Realizar recorridos frecuentes en planta para identificar riesgos, verificar controles y promover comportamientos seguros.
Investigar incidentes, cuasi accidentes y hallazgos, liderando análisis de causa raíz e implementación de acciones correctivas y preventivas.
Actuar como asesor y socio estratégico de la operación, brindando soporte diario a supervisores y colaboradores en la gestión de riesgos EHS.
Identificar riesgos, gestionar auditorías internas y externas, y asegurar el seguimiento efectivo de hallazgos y planes de acción.
Asegurar la correcta ejecución de entrenamientos de seguridad (LOTO, trabajos en alturas, espacios confinados, montacargas, seguridad eléctrica, entre otros).
Supervisar y mantener actualizada la documentación EHS, así como la calidad y confiabilidad de los indicadores (KPIs).
Detener actividades o procesos cuando se detecten condiciones inseguras, actuando con criterio, liderazgo y responsabilidad.
Coordinar planes de respuesta ante emergencias y continuidad del negocio, asegurando la protección de las personas y la operación.
Liderar iniciativas de mejora continua orientadas a fortalecer la cultura de seguridad y el desempeño ambiental de la planta.
Colaborar con equipos multidisciplinarios para integrar requisitos EHS en nuevos proyectos, procesos y cambios operativos.

Lo Que Aportarás

Licenciatura en Ingeniería Industrial, Química, Ambiental o afín.
Experiencia mínima de 3 años en roles de EHS dentro de entornos industriales o de manufactura.
Experiencia demostrada en funciones EHS con alta participación operativa, combinando actividades de campo, liderazgo de equipos, cumplimiento regulatorio y gestión de riesgos.
Conocimiento integral de EHS, abarcando seguridad industrial, salud ocupacional, medio ambiente, preparación ante emergencias, cumplimiento regulatorio y sistemas de gestión, con capacidad para abordar la función desde una perspectiva holística.
Conocimiento sólido de la legislación mexicana en seguridad, salud y medio ambiente.
Experiencia en la implementación y mantenimiento de sistemas de gestión ISO 14001 e ISO 45001.
Capacidad para interactuar con autoridades regulatorias, auditores externos y equipos multifuncionales.
Perfil práctico, orientado a la acción y con presencia en piso, capaz de influir en la operación, tomar decisiones en terreno y liderar iniciativas de mejora continua.

new_jobs.title: Foster Care Case Manager
new_jobs.description:
Company Description
Sunrise Children's Services is a statewide nonprofit organization dedicated to providing care, hope, and therapeutic services to children and families across Kentucky. Since 1869, Sunrise has focused on serving children who have experienced abuse, neglect, and significant trauma and who have been removed from their homes by the state. The organization serves more than 1,000 individuals each day, offering refuge, healing, and support through a network of Christ-centered programs. Licensed as a Behavioral Health Services Organization, Sunrise provides foster care, residential treatment, therapeutic, and community-based services and holds Gold Seal accreditation from The Joint Commission. Applicants can learn more about Sunrise’s mission, programs, and statewide impact at www.sunrise.org.
Role Description
The Foster Care Case Manager is a full-time, on-site role based in Elizabethtown, KY, responsible for supporting children and foster families through comprehensive case management services. Daily responsibilities include assessing child and family needs, developing and updating individualized service plans, and coordinating placements and services with foster parents, schools, medical providers, and community partners. The role involves conducting home visits, monitoring safety and progress, documenting case activities in accordance with agency and regulatory standards, and preparing reports for court and state agencies. The Case Manager provides ongoing support, advocacy, and crisis intervention, facilitating team meetings and ensuring that services align with therapeutic goals and organizational policies. This position collaborates closely with internal clinical staff and external stakeholders to promote positive outcomes and stability for children in care.
Qualifications

Strong case management and social services skills, including assessment, service planning, coordination of care, and advocacy.
Excellent communication and documentation skills, including clear written reports, professional correspondence, and effective interpersonal communication with children, families, and partners.
Organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize multiple cases, maintain accurate records, and meet deadlines and regulatory requirements.
Collaboration and teamwork skills, including the ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams, foster parents, state agencies, and community organizations.
Knowledge of child welfare, trauma-informed care, and behavioral health principles, along with familiarity with foster care regulations and best practices.
Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling, or related human services field; a master’s degree and relevant licensure (e.g., CSW, LCSW) are preferred.
Previous experience in foster care, child welfare, or related residential or community-based services is highly beneficial.
Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel locally for home visits and meetings.
Ability to maintain professional boundaries, uphold confidentiality, and align practice with Sunrise Children’s Services mission and ethical standards.

Overview

Make a difference where it matters most.

The City of Missoula Municipal Court is hiring a Court Case Manager
to play a key role in transforming lives by connecting individuals in the criminal justice system with the support and services they need. If you thrive on building relationships, navigating complex challenges, and advocating for positive change, this position offers a chance to do impactful work every day. From guiding defendants through discharge plans to coordinating mental health, substance use, housing, and vocational resources—you’ll be part of a team working to create safer, healthier outcomes for individuals and the community.

To Apply:

All applicants must submit the City of Missoula application

AND Cover Letter

explaining your interest in this position and detailing how your experience and education meet the qualifications.

Failure to attach the cover letter will result in your application being incomplete, and therefore, not reviewed by the hiring manager.

Priority Screening of applications will begin on Thursday, September 24, 2026.

Applicants applying on or after this date will only be considered if a competitive applicant pool is not received.

Resumes will not be reviewed. All details should be entered on the application.

Starting Pay

New hires start within our entry-to-market range, depending on experience and qualifications.

The starting range for the position is $28.14 - $30.92/hour and will increase each year for longevity and cost of living adjustments.

Full Pay Range

Each position also has a full wage range that reflects potential growth over time, including annual increases for longevity and cost-of-living.

The full range for the position is $28.14 - $32.78/hour.

Essential Functions

Meet directly with defendants pre- and post-sentencing, using established interview techniques and assessment instruments to determine programmatic needs to develop treatment plans and track defendants’ progress.
Provide defendants support through case management and offering information and/or referrals for mental health services, substance use disorder services, and other various programs/resources.
Assist with the Pretrial Assistance to Support Success (PASS) program to coordinate services for defendants’ pre-disposition to support a successful re-entry into the community following release from incarceration.
Establish a collaborative network within the community and other relevant partners to involve family members, community resources, and social service agencies to assist defendants, pre-and post-disposition, with employment and vocational skills, educational and training needs, housing, substance abuse resources, etc.
Assist the Court Program Administrator with community-based programs and other outreach initiatives by attending and providing support to participants and coordinating with other service providers to attend court-sponsored events and provide resources, as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned, based on training and qualifications.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of, or the ability to learn, local substance abuse, mental health services, and community resources, including related government laws and practices of community resources.
Knowledge of general criminal justice and case management practices and procedures, including interviewing and counseling techniques, cultural competence with awareness and respect for diversity and inclusion.
Skill in utilizing various computer software and databases, including Microsoft 365, and the ability to learn job-specific applications and equipment.
Skill in organization, time management and prioritizing with the proven ability to have keen attention to detail and accuracy in performing work with adherence to strict deadlines.
Skill in communicating, in person and writing, with the proven ability to establish and maintain effective working and collaborative relationships with diverse individuals.
Ability to motivate defendants in a positive, constructive manner; facilitating self-determination and self-care through the tenets of advocacy.
Ability to identify and resolve barriers hindering effective program participation and completion for defendants.
Ability to research, analyze, and provide decisive solutions to complex problems and situations.
Ability to maintain current knowledge, developments, and trends related to specific area of focus and/or assigned projects.
Ability to maintain and exhibit integrity and discretion in handling confidential, sensitive, and criminal justice information.
Ability to maintain and foster a culture of professionalism, adhere to departmental and City standards and specifications, and support a positive team environment.
Ability to resolve conflicts with facilitating outcomes while maintaining a calm demeanor.
Ability to learn City and departmental policies, procedures, and practices.

Qualifications And Additional Application Materials

Any combination of education and experience equivalent to four (4) years of experience working or providing case management services in behavioral health care, social services; working in a correctional facility with direct contact with clients, or another relevant field.
Must be able to pass a criminal background check.

new_jobs.title: EHS Supervisor
new_jobs.description:
Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver.

We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. At Vantive, you will become part of a community of people who are focused, courageous and don’t settle for the mediocre. Each of us is driven to help improve patients’ lives worldwide. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities.

Supervisor de EHS

Tu rol en Vantive

En Vantive buscamos un Supervisor de EHS que quiera ser un líder cercano a la operación, con un fuerte sentido de responsabilidad, actitud de servicio y un compromiso genuino con la seguridad, la salud y el medio ambiente.

Esta posición requiere una participación activa y constante en planta, trabajando directamente con los equipos para identificar riesgos, implementar soluciones, resolver situaciones operativas y promover una cultura sólida de seguridad. Buscamos una persona con un enfoque práctico (hands-on), capaz de equilibrar las actividades estratégicas y administrativas con una presencia significativa en piso, liderando con el ejemplo y generando un impacto visible en la operación.

El rol tiene como objetivo asegurar que nuestras operaciones se desarrollen bajo los más altos estándares legales, corporativos y éticos, impulsando una cultura de prevención, cumplimiento y mejora continua que proteja a nuestras personas, nuestras instalaciones y el medio ambiente.

Lo Que Realizarás

Implementar y asegurar el cumplimiento legal y regulatorio en materia de EHS (STPS, SEMARNAT, COFEPRIS), así como de los estándares ISO 14001 e ISO 45001.
Coordinar, ejecutar y dar seguimiento a los programas de EHS en planta, incluyendo contratistas, proveedores, visitantes y colaboradores.
Realizar recorridos frecuentes en planta para identificar riesgos, verificar controles y promover comportamientos seguros.
Investigar incidentes, cuasi accidentes y hallazgos, liderando análisis de causa raíz e implementación de acciones correctivas y preventivas.
Actuar como asesor y socio estratégico de la operación, brindando soporte diario a supervisores y colaboradores en la gestión de riesgos EHS.
Identificar riesgos, gestionar auditorías internas y externas, y asegurar el seguimiento efectivo de hallazgos y planes de acción.
Asegurar la correcta ejecución de entrenamientos de seguridad (LOTO, trabajos en alturas, espacios confinados, montacargas, seguridad eléctrica, entre otros).
Supervisar y mantener actualizada la documentación EHS, así como la calidad y confiabilidad de los indicadores (KPIs).
Detener actividades o procesos cuando se detecten condiciones inseguras, actuando con criterio, liderazgo y responsabilidad.
Coordinar planes de respuesta ante emergencias y continuidad del negocio, asegurando la protección de las personas y la operación.
Liderar iniciativas de mejora continua orientadas a fortalecer la cultura de seguridad y el desempeño ambiental de la planta.
Colaborar con equipos multidisciplinarios para integrar requisitos EHS en nuevos proyectos, procesos y cambios operativos.

Lo Que Aportarás

Licenciatura en Ingeniería Industrial, Química, Ambiental o afín.
Experiencia mínima de 3 años en roles de EHS dentro de entornos industriales o de manufactura.
Experiencia demostrada en funciones EHS con alta participación operativa, combinando actividades de campo, liderazgo de equipos, cumplimiento regulatorio y gestión de riesgos.
Conocimiento integral de EHS, abarcando seguridad industrial, salud ocupacional, medio ambiente, preparación ante emergencias, cumplimiento regulatorio y sistemas de gestión, con capacidad para abordar la función desde una perspectiva holística.
Conocimiento sólido de la legislación mexicana en seguridad, salud y medio ambiente.
Experiencia en la implementación y mantenimiento de sistemas de gestión ISO 14001 e ISO 45001.
Capacidad para interactuar con autoridades regulatorias, auditores externos y equipos multifuncionales.
Perfil práctico, orientado a la acción y con presencia en piso, capaz de influir en la operación, tomar decisiones en terreno y liderar iniciativas de mejora continua.
Habilidad para influir, capacitar, desarrollar conciencia de riesgo y generar compromiso en todos los niveles de la organización.
